title: Wombats Poop Cubes. Scientists Finally Know Why

scenes.text: Wombats poop cubes. Scientists finally figured out how.
A wombat drops up to one hundred of these little cubes a day, each about two centimeters wide.
For years nobody could explain it. The answer was hiding in the last stretch of its gut.
Food takes up to four times longer to pass through a wombat than through you, so by the end it's dry and firm.
Then the last part of the intestine does the shaping. Two stiff sections and two stretchy ones squeeze it into corners.
And the point of a cube? It doesn't roll away. Perfect for leaving a message on top of a rock. What animal should we solve next?

Wombats poop cubes, up to 100 of them a day, each about two centimeters wide.
Researchers found the secret in the last part of the intestine: two stiff and two stretchy sections squeeze the dry waste into corners.
The cubes don't roll away, which helps wombats mark their territory on rocks and logs.
What animal mystery should we solve next?
